name: Famotidine
executiveSummary: H2 antagonist. Adult PO: **20 mg q12h** or **40 mg at night** (ulcer/GERD); IV: **20 mg q12h**. Pediatrics: **0.5 mg/kg/dose q12h** PO/IV (max **40 mg/dose**). Preferred over ranitidine (NDMA).
indications:
## Indications

- GERD, peptic ulcer, hypersecretion; stress-ulcer prophylaxis (IV hospital).
- Alternative when PPI unused or as a bridge.

## Precautions

- Renal impairment: extend interval (e.g. q24–48h by CrCl).
- Fewer CYP interactions than cimetidine; still monitor digoxin/theophylline in special contexts.

> Ranitidine withdrawn/restricted in many markets — **famotidine** or omeprazole are usual substitutes.

adulto.dose: Ulcer/GERD: **20 mg PO q12h** or **40 mg PO at night** × 4–8 weeks. Hypersecretion: up to **20–40 mg q6h**. IV: **20 mg q12h** (infusion or slow).
adulto.administration: PO with or without food. IV: dilute per label; no rapid concentrated bolus.
adulto.notes: Switch to PO when oral route tolerated.

pediatrico.presentation: Tabs; compounded suspension; IV 10–20 mg/mL by brand.
pediatrico.dose: ≥1 y / >10 kg: **0.5 mg/kg/dose PO or IV q12h** (max **40 mg/dose**). Neonates/infants: often **0.5 mg/kg/dose q24h** then q12h — local protocol.
pediatrico.notes: In infant GER prefer non-drug measures first.

neonatal.dose: Guide **0.5 mg/kg/dose** q24h → q12h under NICU.

stability:
## Stability

- Reconstituted IV: per label (hours at room temp).
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Headache, constipation/diarrhea, dizziness; rare: confusion (elderly), IV bradycardia, hepatitis.

bibliography.citation: FDA. Ranitidine NDMA withdrawal — H2 alternatives.
